title: Atomic Theory and Structure - Chemistry - Atomic
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: An atom of Carbon-14 ($^{14}\text{C}$) contains how many neutrons? (Atomic number of Carbon is 6).
questions.explain: The number of neutrons is calculated by $A - Z$, where $(A)$ is the mass number (14) and $(Z)$ is the atomic number (6). $14 - 6 = 8$ neutrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Consider the isotope symbol $^{31}_{15}\text{P}$. What does the number 15 represent?
questions.explain: In the notation $^{A}_{Z}\text{X}$, the subscript $Z$ represents the atomic number (number of protons).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: An atom contains 11 protons, 12 neutrons, and 10 electrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explain: The mass number $(A)$ is the sum of protons and neutrons. $11 + 12 = 23$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following quantities is always equal to the atomic number $(Z)$ of a neutral atom?
questions.explain: For a *neutral* atom, the positive charge of the protons must be balanced by an equal number of negatively charged electrons. Thus, $(Z)$ = number of electrons.
